messages:
emma: quick ping  i pushed a lightweight prototype that publishes compact 'headroom tokens' per pool instead of raw gpu counts. goal: better packing for lots of short inferences and a clear cost signal for routing. draft proto in rfc: https://redwood.internal/rfc/643

josh: neat. two quick questions: how do tokens map to eviction/preemption? and what happens with mixed GPU SKUs?

emma: good Qs. tokens are advisory for admission and soft-eviction scoring only. hard eviction still consults reserved_slots and active_lease metadata. snapshot includes per-sku efficiency factors so tokens -> effective-gpu-units. proto sketch: seq id, ttl, cost_usd_hr, sku_factors, tenant_balances.

kiran: scoring idea? i suggest capping token influence so priorities can't be overridden. e.g., eviction_score = base_priority + preempt_penalty - alpha * min(effective_tokens, cap) + beta * recent_cost_spike.

meera: add safety: every snapshot has seq and ttl; if staleness > threshold scorer ignores tokens. also emit token_staleness metric and a fallback absolute_capacity publish.

josh: ops/UI: show an example mapping like "0.05 token ~= one short chat completion" and expose sku_factor table in the debug view. ops will want a minute-sampled expanded row for SRE without enabling debug everywhere.

emma: agreed. also include reserved_token flag per tenant to protect hard SLAs from token depletion. admission must check sku_compatibility when a tenant has sku constraints.

tom: billing/routing: single authoritative cost_source. routing can read cost_usd_hr but billing must only write when cost_source == operator_master to avoid double-counts.

kiran: rollout checklist: 1) implement proto w/ seq+ttl and sku_factors, 2) capped soft-eviction scorer, 3) token staleness telemetry, 4) canary on canary-2 with synthetic workloads, 5) rollback trigger if eviction_churn > 3x or p95 tail > 1.2x baseline.

meera: test matrix: mostly-short (80/20), mixed-large, and prewarm-burst. measure p50/p95, eviction_count_by_cause, token_staleness_histogram, and billing-read consistency.

emma: i'll add a short example mapping in the RFC and a small operator runbook: how to toggle token scoring per-pool and how to interpret staleness metrics. will tag for review.

autoscaler-bot: Canary scheduled: token-headroom-canary on canary-2 at 2026-03-25T18:00Z. telemetry: token_staleness, eviction_churn, p95_tail.

emma: thanks all. i'll post the RFC follow-up with proto diff, scorer pseudocode, dashboards, and rollback steps. DM me for urgent comments.
